import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 2e-3, "n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.005, "gamma": 0.9, "gae_lambda": 0.85}

STEM = 64
WIDTH = 40
MCH = 8
RED = 16
GH = 64
OUT_GAIN = 0.01


class ChanLN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln = nn.LayerNorm(c)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.ln(x.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, dil):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=dil, dilation=dil)
        self.n = ChanLN(c)
        self.g = nn.Linear(2 * c, c)

    def forward(self, f):
        y = self.conv(f) + self.g(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))[:, :, None, None]
        return F.relu(self.n(f + y))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.X = int(spec.X)
        self.n_place = int(spec.n_place)
        cells = self.Y * self.X
        self.obs_stem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(int(spec.in_channels) + 2, STEM, 1), ChanLN(STEM), nn.ReLU())
        self.mask_emb = nn.Linear(self.n_place, MCH * cells)
        self.mask_ln = ChanLN(MCH)
        self.stem2 = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(STEM + MCH, WIDTH, 1), ChanLN(WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([Block(WIDTH, 1), Block(WIDTH, 1)])
        self.red = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, RED, 1), ChanLN(RED), nn.ReLU())
        self.place_out = nn.Linear(RED * cells, self.n_place)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GH, 1)
        for m in (self.place_out, self.done_head, self.value_head):
            nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=OUT_GAIN)
            nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        Y, X = self.Y, self.X
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        o = self.obs_stem(torch.cat([obs, ys, xs], dim=1))
        m = mask[:, :self.n_place].to(obs.dtype)
        me = F.relu(self.mask_ln(self.mask_emb(m).reshape(B, MCH, Y, X)))
        f = self.stem2(torch.cat([o, me], dim=1))
        for blk in self.blocks:
            f = blk(f)
        place = self.place_out(self.red(f).flatten(1))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 2e-3, "n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.005, "gamma": 0.9, "gae_lambda": 0.85}

H1 = 256
HM = 128
H2 = 256
OUT_GAIN = 0.01


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_place = int(spec.n_place)
        self.n_actions = int(spec.n_actions)
        n_in = int(spec.in_channels) * int(spec.Y) * int(spec.X)
        self.obs_fc = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(n_in, H1), nn.LayerNorm(H1), nn.ReLU())
        self.mask_fc = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(self.n_place, HM), nn.LayerNorm(HM), nn.ReLU())
        self.body = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(H1 + HM, H2), nn.LayerNorm(H2), nn.ReLU(),
                                  nn.Linear(H2, H2), nn.ReLU())
        self.pi = nn.Linear(H2, self.n_actions)
        self.v = nn.Linear(H2, 1)
        for m in (self.pi, self.v):
            nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=OUT_GAIN)
            nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        h = self.obs_fc(obs.reshape(B, -1))
        mh = self.mask_fc(mask[:, :self.n_place].to(obs.dtype))
        z = self.body(torch.cat([h, mh], dim=1))
        return self.pi(z), self.v(z).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no results yet. The starting net scored 0, which matches the program's evidence: most worlds have a mismatch between the frame of the observations and the frame of the actions and mask, or an unusual input scale. Changing only the recipe or the network size has never moved a 0. This round follows step 2 and runs six hedges on the reference recipe: layout set A, layout set B, each of those with the observations fed under all 8 grid symmetries, set A with LayerNorm and output layers initialised at gain 0.01, and set A with symmetries plus LayerNorm. A nonzero score from a set rules in a frame family. A pattern where only the LayerNorm versions score points to a scale problem. If everything scores 0, step 5 applies next round: combined hedges and type-minor layouts. Results are single-seed and bimodal, so a lone 0 is weak evidence.
analyses.2: All six round-1 nets scored 0, including training success, so none of them escaped. The obs-symmetry nets with set A or set B pair the obs under every grid symmetry with one consistent reading of the mask and logits. Between them they cover any dihedral mismatch between the obs and the actions, yet both scored 0, so a simple flip or transpose of the frame is unlikely. LayerNorm with gain-0.01 outputs also scored 0, which argues against a pure scale deviation. One possibility not yet tested is a type-minor action index (cell·K + type). Step 5 of the program tells me to combine hedges next: obs symmetries, LayerNorm, global context in each block and a dilated block. I also add a dense, layout-free hedge: the mask goes in through a Linear embedding and the logits come out of a Linear over the flattened features. That way any permutation of the action indices can be learned. If only that one scores, the action layout is not a grid symmetry.
analyses.3: All 12 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success. The ruled-out cases are these: type-major and type-minor action layouts under all 8 dihedral frames; obs reoriented by any dihedral transform, with or without LayerNorm, global context or a dilated block; and a dense action head over a 1x1-conv obs stem (weak evidence). Four untested causes remain. (1) The obs memory is scrambled in a way that is not a grid symmetry, for example channels-last data read as [C,Y,X]. A 1x1 conv cannot undo that. (2) The action layout is compact (n_place ≠ K·Y·X), so our padding misaligns every type after the first. (3) DONE is at a different index, so the agent cannot finish an exact build. (4) The reward is delayed and needs a long horizon. All conv candidates now detect compact layouts automatically and add a small learned global-to-every-action logit, which hedges (2) and (3) at low cost. Each candidate then tests one obs or recipe hypothesis. An MLP probe that is free of any assumed layout covers arbitrary scrambles.
analyses.4: All 18 trials scored 0, with training success also 0. The hedges ruled out these explanations: all 8 dihedral action frames, alone or combined with any obs symmetry; type-minor layouts; compact layouts; channels-last obs; input scale (LayerNorm); a long horizon with a separate critic; and arbitrary permutations learned by dense heads (weak evidence). Under every hypothesis tested so far, the place and mask readings were consistent with each other. One assumption that was never tested is DONE at the last index. If DONE is really at index 0, our DONE logit lands on a placement that is always illegal (2x2 at the corner). The agent then can never end an episode on purpose, and since every placement adds cells, an exact build is impossible. That matches training success being exactly 0 everywhere. This last round tests DONE-first, with placements shifted by one. A single identity reading plus all 8 obs symmetries covers every obs-versus-action frame without summing layouts.
